source.snippet: We have a new domain. Sending email to Gmail, HotMail results in the messages sent to the Spam folder. I discovered that the static IP address for our email server was blacklisted on spamhaus.org. The IP address was changed to a different address. When I send an email to gmail I find this: (Received: from proxy) and it goes to the Spam folder. I think it should be (Received: from)? How does this get fixed? I don't actually have my own mail server it is outsourced to a hosting provider.

problem_statement: Small business operators launching a new domain find their transactional and outreach email consistently landing in spam due to IP blacklists, misconfigured mail headers, and missing authentication records — costing them leads and revenue while they lack expertise to diagnose and fix it.
target_segment: Small business owners and solo operators who recently acquired a new domain and outsource their email hosting, without in-house technical staff.
notes: Operator is running a business domain (not personal), has already paid for hosting infrastructure, and is blocked from reaching customers. Willingness to pay for a fix is implied by the business context and urgency. This is a recurring class of problem — new domain + outsourced hosting + no technical staff — seen repeatedly across ServerFault, Reddit sysadmin, and support forums. A guided setup wizard or done-for-you deliverability audit service could serve this segment. Signal is low here (single question) but the broader category is well-documented.
